# Customization

## Layouts and responsiveness

`PhotoAlbum` lays out the same photo collection as justified rows, balanced columns, or masonry. All three use intrinsic dimensions and the width of the album container.

## Choose a layout by reading behavior

| Layout    | Placement                                                    | Primary setting   |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------- |
| `rows`    | Groups photos into justified horizontal rows                 | `targetRowHeight` |
| `columns` | Preserves sequence while balancing sequential columns        | `columns`         |
| `masonry` | Places each photo in the current shortest equal-width column | `columns`         |

Rows are the default. Pass the short name when the defaults are enough, or use the object form to configure the selected layout.

```vue [app/pages/gallery.vue]
<template>
  <PhotoAlbum :photos="photos" :layout="{ type: 'rows', targetRowHeight: 240 }" :spacing="8" />
</template>
```

Columns and masonry use the same `columns` setting but produce different visual order and height distribution.

```vue [app/pages/gallery.vue]
<PhotoAlbum :photos="photos" :layout="{ type: 'masonry', columns: 3 }" />
```

## Resolve settings from the container

`spacing`, `padding`, `targetRowHeight`, and `columns` accept a static number or a function of the measured container width. The `responsive()` helper creates a mobile-first resolver from a breakpoint map.

```vue [app/pages/gallery.vue]
<template>
  <PhotoAlbum
    :photos="photos"
    :layout="{
      type: 'columns',
      columns: responsive({ 0: 2, 640: 3, 960: 4 }),
    }"
    :spacing="responsive({ 0: 4, 640: 8, 960: 12 })"
  />
</template>
```

Breakpoint keys are minimum container widths in pixels. At 760px, the example resolves to three columns and 8px spacing regardless of the browser viewport.

The Nuxt module auto-imports `responsive()` by default. Use an explicit import when auto-imports are disabled.

```ts [app/utils/gallery-layout.ts]
import { responsive } from '@nuxt-photo/nuxt/app'

export const gallerySpacing = responsive({
  0: 4,
  640: 8,
  960: 12,
})
```

## Breakpoints also stabilize measurement

`responsive()` attaches its positive breakpoint keys to the resolver. `PhotoAlbum` merges those keys from its responsive settings and snaps the measured width down to the largest matching breakpoint.

You can pass `breakpoints` explicitly when the layout should snap at widths that are not present in a resolver.

```vue [app/pages/gallery.vue]
<PhotoAlbum
  :photos="photos"
  :breakpoints="[640, 960, 1280]"
  :layout="{ type: 'columns', columns: responsive({ 0: 2, 640: 3, 960: 4 }) }"
/>
```

Snapping limits layout recalculation between meaningful widths and gives the server and client values they can share. The [server rendering concept](https://nuxt-photo.lupinum.com/docs/concepts/server-rendering) explains how to choose the initial width.

## Change layout type explicitly

Responsive parameters configure numbers, not the `layout.type` discriminant. Use reactive application state when the layout itself must change.

```vue [app/pages/gallery.vue]
<PhotoAlbum
  :photos="photos"
  :layout="isCompact ? { type: 'masonry', columns: 2 } : { type: 'rows', targetRowHeight: 260 }"
/>
```

Prefer one layout across widths when possible. It preserves a more consistent reading order and reduces visual movement when the container crosses a breakpoint.

_Source: `docs/content/docs/2.concepts/4.layouts-and-responsiveness.md`_

## Server rendering

The server knows each photo's aspect ratio but cannot measure the browser container. Nuxt Photo combines intrinsic dimensions, an optional initial width, and discrete breakpoints to render useful geometry before hydration.

## Intrinsic dimensions are the baseline

Every photo requires a positive `width` and `height`. Nuxt Photo validates those values before layout and uses their ratio in the server-rendered markup.

Keep structure CSS enabled. `css: 'structure'` and `css: 'all'` contain the geometry rules used by albums, carousels, and the lightbox. With `css: 'none'`, the application owns all of those rules.

## Rows render without an assumed width

Rows emit a flex-based server layout from photo aspect ratios. When rows use responsive resolver breakpoints, Nuxt Photo can also emit scoped container rules for the discrete layouts.

```vue [app/pages/gallery.vue]
<PhotoAlbum
  :photos="photos"
  :layout="{
    type: 'rows',
    targetRowHeight: responsive({ 0: 160, 640: 220, 1024: 280 }),
  }"
/>
```

This path produces useful server output without guessing a viewport width. The measured client width still becomes authoritative after mount.

## Columns and masonry benefit from an initial width

Columns and masonry need a width to calculate their final groups. Without one, the server renders a simple grid fallback and the client replaces it with the measured layout after mount.

Set `default-container-width` to a realistic content width when that replacement would be visible above the fold.

```vue [app/pages/gallery.vue]
<PhotoAlbum
  :photos="photos"
  :default-container-width="1024"
  :breakpoints="[640, 1024, 1280]"
  :layout="{
    type: 'columns',
    columns: responsive({ 0: 2, 640: 3, 1024: 4 }),
  }"
/>
```

The server calculates this example at 1024px. After mount, the client snaps the measured container down to the largest matching breakpoint. A 1180px container therefore starts at 1024px too.

If the measured width is below the smallest breakpoint, Nuxt Photo keeps the real width. A value of `0` for `default-container-width` has no effect and produces a development warning.

## Use one shared width strategy

Choose `default-container-width` from the same set passed to `breakpoints`. When `responsive()` supplies the breakpoints automatically, ensure the chosen initial width is one of its keys or pass the complete snap set explicitly.

```vue [app/pages/gallery.vue]
<PhotoAlbum
  :photos="photos"
  :default-container-width="1280"
  :breakpoints="[640, 1024, 1280]"
  :spacing="responsive({ 0: 4, 640: 8, 1024: 12 })"
/>
```

An initial width is an application-shell decision, not a device label. Base it on the actual maximum content column and the widths that dominate production traffic.

## Diagnose visible movement

If an album changes shape after hydration, inspect these causes in order:

1. Confirm every photo has its real intrinsic dimensions.
2. Confirm structure CSS is loaded.
3. Compare the initial width with the resolved client breakpoint.
4. For columns or masonry, add a realistic initial width.
5. Test the page at widths immediately below and above each breakpoint.

For carousels, keep `slideAspect` and photo dimensions stable so the media frame retains its height while Embla attaches client-side behavior.

_Source: `docs/content/docs/2.concepts/5.server-rendering.md`_

## Image pipeline

Every built-in thumbnail and lightbox slide resolves through an image adapter. The adapter receives a `PhotoItem` and either the `thumb` or `slide` context, then returns the final image attributes.

## Choose a provider mode

Configure the app-wide mode under `nuxtPhoto.image`.

| Mode         | Behavior                                                                           |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `auto`       | Uses Nuxt Image when `@nuxt/image` is registered, otherwise uses native attributes |
| `native`     | Uses `src`, `thumbSrc`, and `srcset` without transforming URLs                     |
| `nuxt-image` | Requires `@nuxt/image` and generates provider-backed URLs and candidates           |
| `false`      | Skips module adapter registration so the application can provide one               |

`auto` is the default and keeps Nuxt Image optional.

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@nuxt-photo/nuxt'],
  nuxtPhoto: {
    image: { provider: 'auto' },
  },
})
```

## Native mode preserves supplied sources

For thumbnails, the native adapter uses `thumbSrc` when present and falls back to `src`. For slides, it uses `src` and passes `srcset` through when provided.

```ts [app/data/photos.ts]
export const photos = [
  {
    id: 'coast',
    src: '/photos/coast-2400.jpg',
    thumbSrc: '/photos/coast-480.jpg',
    srcset: '/photos/coast-960.jpg 960w, /photos/coast-1600.jpg 1600w',
    width: 2400,
    height: 1500,
  },
]
```

Choose native mode when the CMS or CDN already returns final URLs and responsive candidates.

## Nuxt Image owns URL generation

Register `@nuxt/image` when thumbnails and slides should use a Nuxt Image provider. Explicit `nuxt-image` mode fails after configured modules finish installing if it is not registered.

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@nuxt-photo/nuxt', '@nuxt/image'],
  nuxtPhoto: {
    image: {
      provider: 'nuxt-image',
      thumb: {
        sizes: 'sm:100vw md:50vw lg:400px',
        quality: 80,
      },
      slide: {
        widths: [640, 960, 1240, 1600],
        maxWidth: 1240,
        quality: 85,
      },
    },
  },
})
```

Nuxt Image provider and remote-domain configuration remains in the top-level `image` block. `nuxtPhoto.image` only controls how Nuxt Photo requests thumbnail and slide variants.

## Custom adapters keep the same contract

An `ImageAdapter` returns `src` and optional `srcset`, `sizes`, `width`, and `height`. Pass it to one recipe with `image-adapter`, or provide it for the application after setting `image: false`.

The [custom image service guide](https://nuxt-photo.lupinum.com/docs/customization/custom-image-service) shows the provider setup and a typed adapter.

A per-component adapter takes precedence over an injected adapter. Without either, `PhotoImage` falls back to the native adapter.

Custom adapters must be deterministic during SSR. The same photo and context must produce the same attributes on the server and client; generate expiring or signed URLs before render rather than from current time or random state inside the adapter.

_Source: `docs/content/docs/2.concepts/6.image-pipeline.md`_

## Lightbox behavior

The lightbox provider owns the active photo, navigation order, zoom state, transitions, gestures, and modal lifecycle. Recipe components create that provider for the common paths.

## Recipes decide who owns the viewer

`PhotoAlbum` creates a lightbox by default. `PhotoGroup` creates one provider for all participating descendants. A standalone `Photo` and `PhotoCarousel` create one only when their `lightbox` prop enables it.

When a recipe is inside an enabled `PhotoGroup`, the group owns the viewer. The descendant contributes its trigger and optional slide renderer instead of creating another provider.

## Transition modes describe the opening source

Set `transition` on the component that owns the provider.

| Mode   | Behavior                                                                     |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `auto` | Uses FLIP when the source thumbnail is sufficiently visible, otherwise fades |
| `flip` | Requests the thumbnail frame and falls back when its geometry is unavailable |
| `fade` | Cross-fades without moving from the thumbnail frame                          |
| `none` | Opens and closes without a transition                                        |

`auto` is the default. It avoids animating from a thumbnail that is mostly outside the viewport or too small to provide a useful source frame. Closing also falls back to a fade when the original thumbnail has unmounted or moved out of view.

```vue [app/pages/gallery.vue]
<PhotoAlbum :photos="photos" :transition="{ mode: 'auto', autoThreshold: 0.6 }" />
```

The operating system reduced-motion preference changes `auto` and `flip` to a fade. Explicit `none` remains instant.

## Input follows the current zoom state

The built-in viewer supports these interactions:

- Arrow keys move between photos, or pan a zoomed image horizontally.
- `Escape` closes the viewer.
- `Z`, double click, or double tap toggles zoom.
- The mouse wheel changes zoom.
- A horizontal drag changes slides when the image is fitted.
- A drag pans a zoomed image; an outward horizontal drag at its edge can change slides.
- A two-pointer gesture pinches to zoom.
- A vertical drag closes a fitted image.
- A single tap toggles the viewer controls.

Navigation commands are ignored while the viewer is closed or a conflicting transition is active. The [programmatic control guide](https://nuxt-photo.lupinum.com/docs/guides/programmatic-lightbox) uses the same controller contract as these built-in inputs.

## The viewer owns modal focus

The recipe `Lightbox` renders a dialog in `body`. While open, it:

- locks body scrolling;
- moves focus into the dialog;
- keeps Tab focus inside its controls;
- marks page siblings inert and hidden from assistive technology;
- restores focus to the opening element after close when that element still exists.

Only one Nuxt Photo provider can own that modal state. Opening a second viewer first closes the active one, then transfers ownership.

## Collection updates preserve identity

If a collection changes while the viewer is open, Nuxt Photo follows the active photo by `id`. Reordering the collection updates its index without changing the visible photo. Removing the active ID closes the viewer because there is no longer a valid slide to own.

## Provider options are setup-time

`lightbox`, `transition`, and `imageAdapter` determine the provider created during component setup. Remount the owner with a new `key` when one of those capabilities must change at runtime.

```vue [app/components/SwitchableGallery.vue]
<PhotoAlbum :key="transitionMode" :photos="photos" :transition="transitionMode" />
```

Reactive photo data can change without a remount because identity is reconciled separately from provider configuration.

_Source: `docs/content/docs/2.concepts/7.lightbox-behavior.md`_

## Customize the recipe lightbox

Wrap the recipe `Lightbox` when its focus management, gestures, zoom, and
transitions are correct but the visible controls need different markup.

```vue [app/components/PortfolioLightbox.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { Lightbox } from '@nuxt-photo/nuxt/app'
</script>

<template>
  <Lightbox>
    <template #counter="{ activeIndex, count }">
      <span>{{ activeIndex + 1 }} / {{ count }}</span>
    </template>

    <template #caption="{ photo }">
      <div v-if="photo">
        <h2 v-if="photo.caption">{{ photo.caption }}</h2>
        <p v-if="photo.description">{{ photo.description }}</p>
      </div>
    </template>

    <template
      #actions="{ prev, next, close, toggleZoom, isZoomedIn, zoomAllowed, controlsDisabled }"
    >
      <button type="button" :disabled="controlsDisabled" @click="prev">Previous</button>
      <button type="button" :disabled="controlsDisabled" @click="next">Next</button>
      <button type="button" :disabled="controlsDisabled || !zoomAllowed" @click="toggleZoom">
        {{ isZoomedIn ? 'Fit image' : 'Zoom image' }}
      </button>
      <button type="button" :disabled="controlsDisabled" @click="close">Close</button>
    </template>
  </Lightbox>
</template>
```

Lightbox navigation loops, so previous and next controls do not need to disable
at the ends of the collection.

Pass the wrapper through the recipe component's `lightbox` prop:

```vue [app/pages/portfolio.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import PortfolioLightbox from '~/components/PortfolioLightbox.vue'
</script>

<template>
  <PhotoAlbum :photos="photos" :lightbox="PortfolioLightbox" />
</template>
```

`lightbox` is selected during provider setup. Remount the album, group, or
carousel when the component choice changes at runtime. Build a [primitive
lightbox](https://nuxt-photo.lupinum.com/docs/customization/custom-lightbox) only when the overlay, viewport,
or control hierarchy itself must change.

_Source: `docs/content/docs/4.customization/2.customize-lightbox.md`_

## Build a custom lightbox

The primitive layer keeps Nuxt Photo state, transitions, gestures, pan, and
zoom while giving you control over the dialog structure. A custom composition
must provide its own accessible name, controls, and layout CSS.

## Create the viewer component

```vue [app/components/PrimitiveLightbox.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import {
  LightboxCaption,
  LightboxControls,
  LightboxOverlay,
  LightboxRoot,
  LightboxSlide,
  LightboxViewport,
} from '@nuxt-photo/nuxt/app'
</script>

<template>
  <LightboxRoot class="np-lightbox" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Photo viewer">
    <LightboxOverlay class="np-lightbox__backdrop" />

    <div class="np-lightbox__ui">
      <LightboxControls
        v-slot="{ activeIndex, count, prev, next, close, controlsDisabled }"
        class="np-lightbox__controls"
      >
        <div class="np-lightbox__topbar">
          <span class="np-lightbox__counter">{{ activeIndex + 1 }} / {{ count }}</span>
          <div class="np-lightbox__actions">
            <button
              class="np-lightbox__btn np-lightbox__btn--prev"
              type="button"
              aria-label="Previous photo"
              :disabled="controlsDisabled"
              @click="prev"
            >
              &larr;
            </button>
            <button
              class="np-lightbox__btn np-lightbox__btn--next"
              type="button"
              aria-label="Next photo"
              :disabled="controlsDisabled"
              @click="next"
            >
              &rarr;
            </button>
            <button
              class="np-lightbox__btn np-lightbox__btn--close"
              type="button"
              aria-label="Close photo viewer"
              @click="close"
            >
              &times;
            </button>
          </div>
        </div>
      </LightboxControls>

      <div class="np-lightbox__stage">
        <LightboxViewport
          v-slot="{ photos, viewportRef, imageLoadFailed }"
          class="np-lightbox__media"
        >
          <div :ref="viewportRef" class="np-lightbox__viewport">
            <div class="np-lightbox__container">
              <LightboxSlide
                v-for="(photo, index) in photos"
                :key="photo.id"
                :photo="photo"
                :index="index"
                class="np-lightbox__slide"
              />
            </div>
          </div>
          <p v-if="imageLoadFailed" class="np-lightbox__fallback" role="status">
            Image could not be loaded.
          </p>
        </LightboxViewport>

        <LightboxCaption v-slot="{ photo }" class="np-lightbox__caption">
          <p v-if="photo?.caption">{{ photo.caption }}</p>
        </LightboxCaption>
      </div>
    </div>
  </LightboxRoot>
</template>
```

The `np-lightbox` classes reuse Nuxt Photo's structural CSS, which the module
loads by default and also includes with `css: 'all'`. Replace those classes
only when you provide equivalent layout rules. `viewportRef` belongs on the
Embla viewport element, whose direct child is the slide container. The
[primitive reference](https://nuxt-photo.lupinum.com/docs/components/lightbox-primitives) documents the slot
contracts and required nesting.

## Use it with a recipe

```vue [app/pages/portfolio.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import PrimitiveLightbox from '~/components/PrimitiveLightbox.vue'
</script>

<template>
  <PhotoAlbum :photos="photos" :lightbox="PrimitiveLightbox" />
</template>
```

`LightboxRoot` teleports to `body`, traps focus, restores focus after closing,
and makes other body children inert while open. Keep `role="dialog"`,
`aria-modal="true"`, and an accessible name on the custom root. Test Escape,
arrow keys, keyboard focus, touch dismissal, zoom, and reduced motion before
replacing the recipe viewer in production.

_Source: `docs/content/docs/4.customization/3.custom-lightbox.md`_

## Integrate a custom image service

An image adapter receives a photo and either the `thumb` or `slide` context. It
returns the attributes for the final `img` element.

```ts [app/utils/photo-adapter.ts]
import type { ImageAdapter, PhotoItem } from '@nuxt-photo/nuxt/app'

const baseUrl = 'https://images.example.com/transform'

function source(photo: PhotoItem, width: number) {
  return `${baseUrl}/${photo.id}?width=${width}&format=webp`
}

export const photoAdapter: ImageAdapter = (photo, context) => {
  const widths = context === 'thumb' ? [480, 960] : [960, 1440, 1920]

  return {
    src: source(photo, widths.at(-1)!),
    srcset: widths.map((width) => `${source(photo, width)} ${width}w`).join(', '),
    sizes: context === 'thumb' ? '(min-width: 960px) 33vw, 100vw' : '100vw',
    width: photo.width,
    height: photo.height,
  }
}
```

Always return `src`. Return dimensions when the final image should keep
intrinsic width and height attributes. Keep the adapter deterministic so SSR
and hydration produce the same URLs; resolve time-sensitive signatures before
rendering rather than calling `Date.now()` in the adapter.

## Provide it to the app

Disable the module-provided adapter, then provide the custom one in a universal
Nuxt plugin.

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@nuxt-photo/nuxt'],
  nuxtPhoto: {
    image: false,
  },
})
```

```ts [app/plugins/photo-adapter.ts]
import { ImageAdapterKey } from '@nuxt-photo/nuxt/app'
import { photoAdapter } from '~/utils/photo-adapter'

export default defineNuxtPlugin((nuxtApp) => {
  nuxtApp.vueApp.provide(ImageAdapterKey, photoAdapter)
})
```

`image: false` skips Nuxt Photo's injected adapter. `PhotoImage` still has a
native fallback, so a missing custom provider renders the original source
rather than disabling images.

## Override one collection

An `image-adapter` prop takes precedence over the injected adapter. Use it when
one collection comes from a different image service.

```vue [app/pages/gallery.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { photoAdapter } from '~/utils/photo-adapter'
</script>

<template>
  <PhotoAlbum :photos="photos" :image-adapter="photoAdapter" />
</template>
```

Test the adapter as a pure function for both contexts and assert the exact
`src`, `srcset`, `sizes`, `width`, and `height` values. The [image pipeline](https://nuxt-photo.lupinum.com/docs/concepts/image-pipeline)
explains adapter precedence and the native and Nuxt Image modes.

_Source: `docs/content/docs/4.customization/4.custom-image-service.md`_
